ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} 
Connect $BC$, \\
given the problem, we have: $OB=OC=BC$, \\
thus, $\triangle OBC$ is an equilateral triangle, \\
hence, $\tan\angle AOC=\tan60^\circ=\boxed{\sqrt{3}}$.

method.method_draft: Use a synthetic geometry route. From the image, note that O, B, A are collinear on the horizontal ray OA, C is the intersection of the two drawn arcs, and ray OC is drawn from O to C. From the text, the first arc is centered at O and passes through B, so OB and OC are radii of the same circle; the second arc is centered at B with radius BO and passes through C, so BC = BO. Therefore OB = OC = BC. Connect BC to form triangle OBC. Since all three sides are equal, triangle OBC is equilateral, so angle BOC is 60 degrees. Because B lies on ray OA, angle AOC equals angle BOC. Hence tan angle AOC = tan 60 degrees = sqrt(3).
